facts.text: The firmware defines 16 degrees of freedom (DOF 16)
The sketch drives up to 16 PWM servos
The serial query token '?' prints the model name and the software version, one per line
The firmware converts the IMU yaw, pitch and roll from radians to degrees before printing
print6Axis prints ypr[1] and ypr[2] as two tab-separated columns followed by a newline
The 'v' token prints the gyro data once
The 'j' handler prints the current joint angles with printTable
printTable prints the joint indices 0 to DOF-1 and then the values separated by a comma and a tab
The joint angle unit of the serial commands is degree
The 'd' token puts the robot down and shuts down the servos
The rest handler in the firmware calls pwm.shutServos() and the firmware then echoes the command token
Lowercase serial commands are terminated by a newline
The firmware echoes the command token after the reply (postures and other tokens confirm completion that way)
The serial monitor is set to no line ending at 115200 baud
The Python API opens the serial port with Communication(p, 115200, 1)
